text: me_on = me_on or hub.par.Solo.eval() or hub.par.Scene.eval() == parent().name

const1value.expr: (float(parent().par.Phase) if parent().par.Manual else (lambda q, n: (math.floor(q*n)/n if n > 0.5 else q))(min(1.0, ((float(op('hub')['bar_pos'])/float(op('tk')['cyc'])) % 1.0)/max(1e-3, 1.0-float(op('tk')['rest']))), float(op('tk')['stepq'])))

const4value.expr: float(op('tk')['tgtx']) + (float(op('tk')['dist'])*(1.0 + 0.22*max(0.0, 1.0 - float(op('shot')['age'])/0.5)**2)*(1.0 - 0.025*float(op('hub')['pulse']) - 0.03*min(float(op('hub')['hit_low']), 1.3)))*math.sin((lambda u: math.radians(float(op('tk')['az']) + min(float(op('tk')['swing']), 18.0 if u else 1e9)*math.sin(float(op('hub')['evolve'])*0.35 + float(op('shot')['seed'])*6.283) + (0.0 if u else float(op('tk')['orbit'])*float(op('hub')['evolve'])) + (float(op('shot')['seed'])-0.5)*min(float(op('tk')['azseed']), 50.0 if u else 1e9)))((1.0 if (float(op('modes')['input']) > 0.5 and float(op('tk')['insub']) >= 0) else 0.0) > 0.5))

const6value.expr: float(op('tk')['tgtz']) + (float(op('tk')['dist'])*(1.0 + 0.22*max(0.0, 1.0 - float(op('shot')['age'])/0.5)**2)*(1.0 - 0.025*float(op('hub')['pulse']) - 0.03*min(float(op('hub')['hit_low']), 1.3)))*math.cos((lambda u: math.radians(float(op('tk')['az']) + min(float(op('tk')['swing']), 18.0 if u else 1e9)*math.sin(float(op('hub')['evolve'])*0.35 + float(op('shot')['seed'])*6.283) + (0.0 if u else float(op('tk')['orbit'])*float(op('hub')['evolve'])) + (float(op('shot')['seed'])-0.5)*min(float(op('tk')['azseed']), 50.0 if u else 1e9)))((1.0 if (float(op('modes')['input']) > 0.5 and float(op('tk')['insub']) >= 0) else 0.0) > 0.5))

index.expr: (1 + (int(op('shot')['take']) % 10 + (10 if op('ctl')['useinp'] > 0.5 else 0))) if float(op('modes')['describe']) > 0.5 else 0

pars.text:
SHATTER AND REASSEMBLE: A 3D MODEL CUT INTO ABOUT A DOZEN BIG PIECES BEFORE PLAYBACK
A shader pushes the pieces apart and pulls them back, whole on every bar line. Kick drums open the cracks.

FORTY COPIES OF ONE PRE-CUT MODEL, EACH IN ABOUT 40 SHARDS
A burst wave crosses the grid every two bars. Each shard's path is a formula of the bar phase, so it reverses exactly.

SHATTER AND REASSEMBLE: THE INPUT PICTURE ON A SLAB CUT INTO A DOZEN BIG PIECES
A shader pushes the pieces apart and pulls them back, whole on every bar line. Kick drums open the cracks.

FORTY COPIES OF THE INPUT PICTURE, EACH ON A SLAB PRE-CUT INTO 40 SHARDS
A burst wave crosses the grid every two bars. Each shard's path is a formula of the bar phase, so it reverses exactly.

KNOLLING: THE INPUT PICTURE ON A SLAB, TAKEN APART INTO ITS 260 PRE-CUT PIECES
Each piece hops to a slot in a grid, turns its skin up and scales to fit, then flies home. One cycle is two bars.

THE INPUT PICTURE ON A SLAB CUT INTO NEARLY 5,000 CHIPS, DITHERED TO BLACK AND WHITE
The chips ride a flow field, then lock in from left to right and hold for one bar.

SEVEN GILDED COPIES OF THE INPUT PICTURE; THE FLOOR REFLECTION IS A MIRRORED COPY
They crack open one after another down the line, once every two bars. Vocals brighten the white insides.

THE INPUT PICTURE ON A SLAB SLICED ON HORIZONTAL PLANES, TEN SLICES PER UNIT OF HEIGHT
The slabs slide apart from the top down and close again once per bar. Kick drums nudge them open.

THE INPUT PICTURE ON GLASS SHARDS, DRAWN ADDITIVELY WITH NO DEPTH TEST
Rims, highlights and the picture add up to brightness. The slab opens and closes over two bars.

THE INPUT PICTURE ON A SLAB CUT INTO 260 BLOCKS
The blocks fall from the top down, then the same motion runs backwards. One fall and rise takes two bars.

THE CAMERA SITS INSIDE ONE BURST OF THE INPUT PICTURE THAT LASTS FOUR BARS
Nothing is simulated: each shard's position is a formula of the bar phase, so every piece returns to its place.

THE INPUT PICTURE ON A LIT SLAB AND ITS SHADOW, DITHERED TO PURE BLACK AND WHITE
The burst phase is rounded to twelve steps per burst, which gives the stop-motion look.

KNOLLING: ONE MODEL TAKEN APART INTO ITS 260 PRE-CUT PIECES
Each piece hops to a slot in a grid, turns its skin up and scales to fit, then flies home. One cycle is two bars.

A 3D SENTENCE CUT INTO NEARLY 5,000 CHIPS, DRAWN IN PURE BLACK AND WHITE
The chips ride a flow field, then lock in from left to right and hold for one bar.

SEVEN GILDED COPIES OF ONE PRE-CUT MODEL; THE FLOOR REFLECTION IS A MIRRORED COPY
They crack open one after another down the line, once every two bars. Vocals brighten the white insides.

ONE MODEL SLICED ON HORIZONTAL PLANES, TEN SLICES PER UNIT OF HEIGHT
The slabs slide apart from the top down and close again once per bar. Kick drums nudge them open.

THE SAME SHARDS DRAWN ADDITIVELY WITH NO DEPTH TEST
Only edge-on rims and highlights add up to brightness, so the object reads as glass. It opens and closes over two bars.

EXTRUDED 3D TEXT CUT INTO HUNDREDS OF BLOCKS
The blocks fall from the top down, then the same motion runs backwards. One fall and rise takes two bars.

THE CAMERA SITS INSIDE ONE BURST THAT LASTS FOUR BARS
Nothing is simulated: each shard's position is a formula of the bar phase, so every piece returns to its place.

ONE LIT MODEL AND ITS SHADOW, DITHERED TO PURE BLACK AND WHITE
The burst phase is rounded to twelve steps per burst, which gives the stop-motion look.
